turns.user: I've just been put on beta blockers, how should I change my training
turns.reply:
Being prescribed beta blockers is a significant change, so we want to make sure we adjust how you track your effort safely. 

Because beta blockers explicitly blunt your heart rate, any heart rate zones on a watch or tracker won't align with how hard your body is actually working anymore. For your lifting and any cardio, you should shift entirely to using RPE (Rate of Perceived Exertion) on a 1-to-10 scale to gauge your effort, rather than relying on heart rate or pre-set percentage targets. 

Since this is a prescription medication, you need to have a quick chat with your doctor or pharmacist about how this specific blocker affects your exercise tolerance, and what they recommend as a safe ceiling for your physical exertion. 

Once you've had that conversation, let me know what they say. We can easily adjust the volume or intensity of your sessions here to match whatever parameters they set for you.

turns.user: I know you can't prescribe, just tell me roughly what to expect
turns.reply:
The main thing to expect is a noticeable ceiling on how high your heart rate can go, which will make your body feel a bit different during training. 

Here is what usually happens when you lift or do cardio on beta blockers:

1. A feeling of hitting a "governor": When you push hard—like during a heavy set of squats or a sprint—you might feel like you've run out of gas sooner than usual. Your heart simply cannot pump faster to meet the high oxygen demand, so you'll feel fatigued or slightly winded at lower workloads.
2. Slower recovery between sets: Because your heart rate is kept low, it takes longer to clear metabolic waste and deliver fresh oxygen to your muscles. You will likely need to extend your rest periods between sets to get your breathing back under control.
3. Mild dizziness when standing up quickly: Beta blockers lower blood pressure. If you go from a lying or seated lift (like a bench press or leg press) to standing up too fast, you might feel a brief head rush. Taking an extra moment to sit up before standing will prevent this.

Because of this, your working weights might need to come down a bit initially, and that is completely normal. 

How has your energy been feeling overall since you started taking them?
